title: Lock out a ball valve: close a clamshell lockout around its lever and slide its lock bar through
instruction: Close the red clamshell around the valve's yellow lever, slide the steel bar through both holes until it rests in them, then let go.
context: Lockout/tagout on a lever ball valve. General maintenance and repair workers (BLS 49-9071, about 1.5 million US jobs) and industrial machinery mechanics (BLS 49-9041, about 0.4 million) apply a lock to every valve they isolate before servicing a line, a duty set by OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 that recurs at each shutdown. The two clamshell halves are spring-opened, so they must be held shut around the lever while the lock bar is pushed through the end plates' holes, which line up only when both halves are shut. The ability is holding two sprung halves shut by hand while a bar is pushed through them; no latch, screw or padlock does it.
setup: Station table; positions in metres, x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up; the table top is at z 0.7475. (1) Lever ball valve (fixed): brass body 40 x 36 x 34 mm (x, y, z) on a 21.4 mm brass pipe stub 200 mm long running along x, 1.0 kg with its stands and base, colour sRGB (0.78, 0.60, 0.25), stem centred at (0.170, 0.090); the pipe axis is 0.027 m above the table, held by two grey stand blocks 14 x 30 x 16 mm (x, y, z). A grey ABS base plate 44 x 100 x 11 mm (x, y, z), colour (0.30, 0.30, 0.32), bolted to the body by a bracket, lies under the clamshell from y 0.086 to -0.014 with its top at z 0.8075. (2) Lever: yellow steel, 95 x 20 x 4 mm, 50 g, colour (0.95, 0.78, 0.10), on the vertical stem at z 0.8225; it lies shut along y from y 0.100 to 0.005 (pointing toward the right arm) and turns about the stem against 1.2 N m of friction (about 13 N at the lever tip). (3) Clamshell lockout: two red ABS halves, colour (0.80, 0.12, 0.10), 60 g each, one each side of the lever, hinged on horizontal pins along y at z 0.8085, at x 0.183 (half A) and x 0.157 (half B). Each half is a wall 3 x 100 x 28 mm (y 0.086 to -0.014) plus a 5 mm end plate 29 x 28 mm with a 10.5 mm square hole at the lever's height (plate A at y -0.014 to -0.019, plate B at y -0.019 to -0.024), so the holes lie on the line x 0.170, z 0.8225. A spring (0.10 N m/rad) holds each half open at 38 deg; shut (0 deg, the stop) the walls stand 1.5 mm from the lever's sides and the two holes coincide. (4) Lock bar: steel, 8 x 8 x 60 mm with a red 16 x 16 x 4 mm cap, 43 g, colour (0.62, 0.63, 0.67), lying along y on the rib, tip toward the valve, centre (0.170, -0.100, 0.7635), tip at y -0.070. (5) Bar rib (fixed): dark grey polyethylene, 6 x 35 x 12 mm (x, y, z), centre (0.170, -0.100), on the table.
scoring: Whole-run record (a linkkit History updated every control step, cleared only by the simulator reset). Measured: the lever's angle from shut; each half's angle from its stop; the bar's tip, centring in both holes at the plates' mid-planes and tilt from the clamshell axis, all from the bar's pose; the grippers' openings, pad clearances and speeds. Gate, any time in the run, gives 0: the lever turned 5 deg from shut. Shut = both halves within 6 deg of their stops. Through = bar tip at least 5 mm past the second plate's far face (the y -0.014 side), centred within 3 mm in both holes, within 20 deg of the clamshell axis. Ladder: 0.25 = the held bar's tip passed the first plate's hole at some time; 0.5 = shut and through at some time; 0.75 = shut and through at the end; 1.0 = shut and through for the last 2 s with the bar under 3 mm/s and 3 deg/s and the halves under 1 deg/s, and both grippers at least 30 mm from the valve and bar and under 5 mm/s for the last 1 s (release gate). success() is the 1.0 rung and must hold 1 s. Real trial: a degree scale taped at the stem for the lever turn; a 3 mm feeler gauge at each wall top for shut (6 deg); a steel rule for the bar's tip beyond the far plate and its centring; a protractor for the bar's tilt; 60 fps video on a fixed tripod for stillness and clearance, read by comparing two frames 2 s apart against a taped steel rule and a protractor: the bar's tail cap moved under 6 mm along the rule and turned under 6 deg, each wall top moved under 2 mm; and, in the frame 1 s from the end, every part of both grippers at least 30 mm from the valve and bar on the rule and each gripper moved under 5 mm in the last second.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lay the bar on its rib along y with its tip toward the valve and its cap toward the right arm; let both halves spring open to their 38 deg stops; set the lever shut (along y, against the stop mark) and check it turns only above 1.2 N m (a spring scale hooked at the lever tip, 90 mm from the stem, reads about 13 N).
fidelity: Rigid ABS halves on pin hinges with torsion springs; the lock bar is a steel square-section lock bar (8 x 8 mm) in square holes with 1.25 mm play. The bar rests tilted by its play (about 13 deg) once released. Lever stem friction is 1.2 N m, in the range of a 1/2 inch lever ball valve. Pipe, stand and base are fixed.
